tool_input.args: Apply the full figure checklist to this figure (panels a-g, a schematic/example figure illustrating image formatting best practices). Figure caption: "a–c, Image formatting may include image cropping, rotation and resizing (a), image spacing in the figure (b) and presenting several magnifications (zoom, inset) of images (c). d–g, Image colors and channels. d, Adjust brightness and/or contrast to achieve good visibility of the imaging signal. e, Channel information should be annotated and visible to audiences (high contrast to background color, visible to color-blind audiences). f, Image details are most unbiased in grayscale. g, It is best practice to publish legends for color intensities (intensity and/or calibration scales) with images, and this is recommended for pseudocolor scales."

Check every panel (a-g) of this figure for micrograph scale bars. Panel a: schematic image cropping diagram with cartoon icons plus a microscopy image with cyan/magenta/green channels and a scale bar visible in lower left of each cropped image. Panel b: cartoon cell diagrams plus two fluorescence microscopy images side by side (labeled A and B) with scale bars. Panel c: cartoon diagram plus fluorescence microscopy image (A) with inset (A') showing zoomed region with arrowheads, both with scale bars. Panel d: grayscale microscopy images (egg-like oocyte structure) in three brightness/contrast versions, each with a scale bar. Panel e: four microscopy images (Marker 1, Marker 2, merge, and histology staining) each with scale bars. Panel f: merge and grayscale channel images of oocyte, each with scale bars. Panel g: two microscopy images (grayscale intensity and pseudocolor) each with scale bars and calibration legends showing intensity values (2,832 to 165). Figure caption does not explicitly state scale bar lengths in text. Determine for each panel whether it's a micrograph, whether scale bar is present, and whether it's defined (length stated) in caption or on image.

Check panels a-g of this figure for whether any panel is a plot showing averages that would require individual data points. Panel a: schematic diagram + microscopy images about cropping. Panel b: schematic diagram + microscopy images about spacing. Panel c: schematic diagram + microscopy images about insets. Panel d: grayscale microscopy images illustrating brightness/contrast adjustment. Panel e: schematic circles (Aa) illustrating color contrast/colorblind visibility + microscopy images. Panel f: schematic venn-diagram-like icons + microscopy images illustrating grayscale channels. Panel g: schematic gradient bar diagrams + microscopy images with calibration scale legends (Max/Min, numeric values). None of these panels are bar charts, scatter plots, or statistical plots with averages - they are all schematic illustrations and example micrographs for a methods/guideline figure.

Check panels a-g of this figure for error bars or box/violin plot elements. Panel a: schematic diagram + microscopy images about cropping/rotation/resizing. Panel b: schematic diagram + microscopy images about image spacing. Panel c: schematic diagram + microscopy images about insets/zoom. Panel d: grayscale microscopy images illustrating brightness/contrast adjustment with a Min-Max slider bar graphic (not a data error bar, it's an illustrative slider). Panel e: schematic circles (Aa) + microscopy images illustrating channel annotation contrast. Panel f: schematic venn-diagram icons + microscopy images illustrating grayscale channels. Panel g: schematic gradient bar diagrams + microscopy images with calibration legends (Max/Min numeric scale bars for intensity, not statistical error bars). None of these panels are statistical plots with error bars or box/violin plots - they are schematic illustrations and example micrographs for a methods/guideline figure about image formatting best practices.
